en.text:
Today’s M&A briefing — 3 deals, the strategies behind them · 20 October 2026

🔹 Merck KGaA (science and technology group, Darmstadt, Germany) acquires Silence Therapeutics plc (siRNA therapies targeting rare and cardiovascular diseases, Nasdaq-listed, headquartered in London) — $20.
The core asset is Divesiran, a Phase 3 siRNA therapy for polycythemia vera, administered via quarterly subcutaneous injection, which achieved an 88% responder rate versus 19% for placebo in Phase 2.
Our view: Merck KGaA is essentially paying for a single Phase 3 molecule in a rare indication with high unmet need, continuing a pipeline acquisition strategy previously seen with SpringWorks Therapeutics.

🔹 Construction Partners Inc (road and surface civil infrastructure construction, repair, and maintenance, Southeastern and Central US) acquires S.E. Cline Construction Inc (commercial site development and underground utility construction, I-95 corridor, Northeast and Central Florida).
The transaction adds approximately 60 employees and a rail-served hot-mix asphalt plant in Bunnell, Florida. Operations will integrate into C.W.
Our view: A rail-served asphalt plant on I-95 is a production asset that reduces supplier dependence and improves margins on local public works projects.

🔹 Platinum Equity (US private equity firm specializing in industrial operations and equipment) takes a majority stake in Trime (mobile lighting towers, generators, and security towers in conventional, hybrid, battery, and solar versions).
Trime operates four production sites in Italy and sells in over 30 countries, with direct operations in the UK, Netherlands, US, and Australia. The founder, CEO, and other management members are reinvesting alongside Platinum. Closing expected in early 2027.
Our view: Platinum Equity is acquiring an Italian production base to address structural US demand for construction lighting equipment, driven by infrastructure and data center investments.

🔹 Merck KGaA (𝑔𝑟𝑜𝑢𝑝𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑠𝑐𝑖𝑒𝑛𝑐𝑒𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑡𝑒𝑐ℎ𝑛𝑜𝑙𝑜𝑔𝑖𝑒𝑠, 𝐷𝑎𝑟𝑚𝑠𝑡𝑎𝑑𝑡, 𝐴𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑚𝑎𝑔𝑛𝑒) rachète Silence Therapeutics plc (𝑡ℎ𝑒́𝑟𝑎𝑝𝑖𝑒𝑠 𝐴𝑅𝑁𝑠𝑖 𝑐𝑖𝑏𝑙𝑎𝑛𝑡 𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑚𝑎𝑙𝑎𝑑𝑖𝑒𝑠 𝑟𝑎𝑟𝑒𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑐𝑎𝑟𝑑𝑖𝑜𝑣𝑎𝑠𝑐𝑢𝑙𝑎𝑖𝑟𝑒𝑠, 𝑐𝑜𝑡𝑒́𝑒 𝑎𝑢 𝑁𝑎𝑠𝑑𝑎𝑞, 𝑠𝑖𝑒̀𝑔𝑒 𝑎̀ 𝐿𝑜𝑛𝑑𝑟𝑒𝑠) — 20 $.
L'actif central est Divesiran, thérapie ARNsi en phase 3 pour la polycythémie vera, administrée par injection sous-cutanée trimestrielle, ayant atteint 88 % de répondeurs contre 19 % pour le placebo en phase 2.
Point de vue : Merck KGaA paie essentiellement pour une seule molécule en phase 3 dans une indication rare à fort besoin non satisfait, poursuivant une logique d'acquisition de pipeline déjà suivie avec SpringWorks Therapeutics.

🔹 Construction Partners Inc (𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑢𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛, 𝑟𝑒́𝑝𝑎𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑒𝑡 𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑟𝑒𝑡𝑖𝑒𝑛 𝑑𝑒 𝑟𝑜𝑢𝑡𝑒𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑖𝑛𝑓𝑟𝑎𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑢𝑐𝑡𝑢𝑟𝑒𝑠 𝑐𝑖𝑣𝑖𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑠𝑢𝑟𝑓𝑎𝑐𝑒, 𝑠𝑢𝑑-𝑒𝑠𝑡 𝑒𝑡 𝑐𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑟𝑒 𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝐸́𝑡𝑎𝑡𝑠-𝑈𝑛𝑖𝑠) rachète S.E. Cline Construction Inc (𝑑𝑒́𝑣𝑒𝑙𝑜𝑝𝑝𝑒𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡 𝑑𝑒 𝑠𝑖𝑡𝑒𝑠 𝑐𝑜𝑚𝑚𝑒𝑟𝑐𝑖𝑎𝑢𝑥 𝑒𝑡 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑢𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑒 𝑟𝑒́𝑠𝑒𝑎𝑢𝑥 𝑠𝑜𝑢𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑟𝑎𝑖𝑛𝑠, 𝑐𝑜𝑟𝑟𝑖𝑑𝑜𝑟 𝐼-95, 𝑛𝑜𝑟𝑑-𝑒𝑠𝑡 𝑒𝑡 𝑐𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑟𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑙𝑎 𝐹𝑙𝑜𝑟𝑖𝑑𝑒).
L'opération apporte environ 60 employés et un site de production d'enrobé bitumineux à chaud desservi par voie ferrée à Bunnell (Floride). Les activités seront intégrées à C.W.
Point de vue : Un site d'enrobé desservi par voie ferrée sur l'I-95 est une infrastructure de production qui réduit la dépendance aux fournisseurs et améliore les marges sur les chantiers publics locaux.

🔹 Platinum Equity (𝑓𝑜𝑛𝑑𝑠 𝑎𝑚𝑒́𝑟𝑖𝑐𝑎𝑖𝑛 𝑑𝑒 𝑝𝑟𝑖𝑣𝑎𝑡𝑒 𝑒𝑞𝑢𝑖𝑡𝑦 𝑠𝑝𝑒́𝑐𝑖𝑎𝑙𝑖𝑠𝑒́ 𝑑𝑎𝑛𝑠 𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝑜𝑝𝑒́𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑠 𝑖𝑛𝑑𝑢𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝑒́𝑞𝑢𝑖𝑝𝑒𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑠) prend une participation majoritaire dans Trime (𝑡𝑜𝑢𝑟𝑠 𝑑'𝑒́𝑐𝑙𝑎𝑖𝑟𝑎𝑔𝑒 𝑚𝑜𝑏𝑖𝑙𝑒𝑠, 𝑔𝑒́𝑛𝑒́𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑒𝑢𝑟𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑡𝑜𝑢𝑟𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑠𝑒́𝑐𝑢𝑟𝑖𝑡𝑒́ 𝑒𝑛 𝑣𝑒𝑟𝑠𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑠 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑣𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑒, ℎ𝑦𝑏𝑟𝑖𝑑𝑒, 𝑏𝑎𝑡𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑖𝑒 𝑒𝑡 𝑠𝑜𝑙𝑎𝑖𝑟𝑒).

Point de vue : Platinum Equity rachète une base de production italienne pour adresser la demande américaine structurelle en équipements d'éclairage de chantier, portée par les investissements dans les infrastructures et les centres de données.

Today’s fundraising briefing — 3 deals, the strategies behind them · 20 October 2026

🔹 Tenstorrent (open-architecture, open-weight AI chip design and associated software tools, Canada) — $6.2bn · Series E.
Post-money valuation reaches $6.2 billion, more than double the $2.6 billion from the Series D in late 2024. Tenstorrent is led by Jim Keller, a recognized processor architect in the industry.
Our view: The entry of public asset managers (Morgan Stanley, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, ARK Invest) into a private round signals that Tenstorrent is preparing for an IPO and that the Nvidia alternative thesis is now treated as a credible portfolio position.

🔹 Linkener (software platform for consumption measurement, data analysis, and AI for corporate energy management, Spain) — €7.5m.
Use of funds: Product development, proprietary AI models, acquisitions.
Investors: Klima Energy Transition Fund (Alantra's energy transition fund, lead investor); GoHub Ventures (existing investor).

🔹 Huppa (all-in-one management platform for gyms, CrossFit boxes, yoga, Pilates, and martial arts studios, Amsterdam) — €1m · Pre-seed.
Founded in 2024 by Sharief Mohamed and Gino Arendsz, the platform centralizes members, classes, payments, reporting, and access controls, with integrations for Mollie, Urban Sports Club, and ClassPass.
Use of funds: Platform development, team expansion, addition of AI analytics and automation capabilities.
